## Source, scope, and table structure

The exact Sylven Arc source is f7f7868561b86f4f0db6423413f626355b57639e. Its direct phase chain has seven single-parent commits and zero merges, preserving the first final and four corrections. The original 43,321-word baton and four correction supplements were read through EOF before owner repository mutation. Repeated identical catalogue clauses were factored losslessly; every distinct clause and every contract field was read and reconstructed.

A complete table is a finite object with declared state and alphabet sets. This operation counts those sets and their transition entries after validating every destination. A missing transition is refused, because silently inventing a sink state would change the input contract. The count is about a supplied representation; it does not measure a physical system or establish a governing policy.

Dynamic counts advance one symbol-length layer at a time. Every transition contributes the number of words that reached its source; accepting-state counts are summed only at the requested length. Boolean values, negative lengths, fractions, and lengths beyond the declared bound are refused. Large exact integers remain counts of supplied formal words and are never treated as observed throughput, probability, or performance.

Shortlex enumeration orders words first by length and then by the sorted alphabet. The request carries a maximum length, and the implementation checks the total enumeration budget before generating candidates. Every result states its finite coverage explicitly. A list of accepted sample words does not establish unbounded equivalence, completeness of an external protocol, or the absence of longer counterexamples.

Breadth-first state search finds a shortest accepted word, using alphabet order to make ties deterministic. A null witness means the declared table accepts no word; an empty string means the initial state already accepts. Those are different outcomes. The search records only formal language structure and supplies no evidence about elapsed real time, operator effort, or optimal physical control.

Equivalence searches the complete reachable product of two supplied tables with the same alphabet. A state pair with different acceptance bits gives a counterexample word. Exhausting that finite product supports equality of the two declared languages. This is stronger than a bounded word sample, while remaining a statement about those exact tables and never about independently observed systems or real deployment behavior.

Language inclusion uses the same finite product but looks specifically for a word accepted on the left and rejected on the right. Direction matters: swapping operands changes the question. The returned counterexample preserves that orientation. An inclusion result cannot transfer ownership, permissions, rights, or trust from one record to another; those are separate evidence and authority obligations.

Disjointness asks whether any product state accepts on both sides. If the empty word is shared, the counterexample is the empty string rather than a missing value. Otherwise breadth-first search supplies the earliest shortlex shared word. Shared syntax is not evidence of shared identity, common provenance, consent, or independent corroboration; the operation has no authority to make those substitutions.

Intersection membership reports conjunction for one word and preserves both operand results. A false intersection can arise because either or both operands reject. Those possibilities remain visible in the envelope. The calculation does not constitute agreement by two independent reviewers: the tables are synthetic, the owner is shared, and some comparison packages themselves share implementation lineage.

Difference membership preserves left-minus-right orientation. The result is true only when the left table accepts and the right table rejects. No source record is removed and no negative is erased by this operation. The term difference describes formal membership, not permission to delete artifacts, revoke an identity, alter a right, or rewrite an earlier receipt.

Textual transition lines preserve the source labe
